title: First absolute moment bound from tail control
statement: Let $\\nu$ and $\\tau$ be finite measures on $\\mathbb R$ with integrable absolute-value functions, and let $B:\\mathbb R\\to\\mathbb R$ be integrable on $(0,\\infty)$. If for every $t>0$ the absolute difference between $\\nu(\\{x:|x|>t\\})$ and $\\tau(\\{x:|x|>t\\})$ is at most $B(t)$, then the absolute difference between their first absolute moments is at most $\\int_0^\\infty B(t)\\,dt$.
hypotheses_covered: $\\nu$ and $\\tau$ are finite measures on $\\mathbb R$
$x\\mapsto |x|$ is integrable with respect to each measure
